subproblem.title: Closed top-degree currents annihilate (D_j a) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ (Step 2 of Simon 2.34)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n = m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set and T ∈ D_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) with ∂T = 0. If a : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C^∞ with compact support and spt a ⊆ U, j ∈ {1,…,n}, and ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) satisfies ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n) = D_j a(x) for every x ∈ ℝⁿ (i.e. ω = (D_j a) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ), then T(ω) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), T.boundary = 0 → ∀ (a : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → tsupport a ⊆ U → ∀ (j : Fin (m + 1)) (ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1)), (∀ x, (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) = fderiv ℝ a x (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) → T ω = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34, printed proof (p. 143): the forms ω_j = (−1)^{j−1} a dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{j−1}∧dx^{j+1}∧⋯∧dxⁿ, the observation dω_j = (D_j a) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ, and display (2) T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0; together with the algebraic fact of Step 1 of the parent proof (every n-covector on ℝⁿ is a multiple of dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ). Here the printed computation is carried out for a test function a (Step 2 of the parent proof).

Setting and notation. m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ an arbitrary set (no openness is needed), T ∈ D_n(U) (Lean: T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)) with ∂T = 0 (Lean: T.boundary = 0, where (∂T)(η) = T(dη), `GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply`). e = (e_0,…,e_m) is the standard basis of ℝⁿ (Lean: e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1; indices are 0-based in Lean, i.e. Lean index j corresponds to the book's j+1). D_j a(x) := Da(x)(e_j) (Lean: fderiv ℝ a x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)). a : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport a ⊆ U; ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) satisfies ω(x)(e) = D_j a(x) for all x ∈ ℝⁿ. Claim: T(ω) = 0.

Proof.

1. (The volume covector.) Let dx := dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ be the n-covector v = (v_0,…,v_m) ↦ det[v_0 … v_m] (coordinates w.r.t. e). In Lean this is the continuous alternating map whose underlying alternating map is (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det; it is continuous because v ↦ det of the coordinate matrix of v is continuous (`Continuous.matrix_det` with the continuous coordinate functionals). dx(e) = 1 (`Module.Basis.det_self`).

2. (Fact A: top-degree covectors.) Every α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) (Lean: α : Covector (Eucl n) n) satisfies α = α(e)·dx. Indeed the alternating n-linear forms on the n-dimensional space ℝⁿ form a one-dimensional space spanned by the determinant, and comparing values at e gives the coefficient; in Mathlib this is `AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det` applied to α.toAlternatingMap and the standard basis.

3. (The (n−1)-form ω_j of the printed proof.) Let ι_j ∈ Λ^m(ℝⁿ) be the interior product ι_j(w_1,…,w_m) := dx(e_j, w_1, …, w_m) (Lean: `ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft` of dx at e_j, so ι_j(w) = dx(Fin.cons e_j w)). Expanding the determinant along its first column (which is e_j) shows ι_j = (−1)^{j'−1} dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{j'−1}∧dx^{j'+1}∧⋯∧dxⁿ with j' = j+1 the book's 1-based index; thus η := a·ι_j, i.e. η(x) := a(x)·ι_j, is exactly the printed form ω_j. η is C^∞ (a smooth scalar function times a constant covector), tsupport η ⊆ tsupport a, which is compact and contained in U. Hence η ∈ D^m(U) (Lean: an element of TestFormOn U m).

4. (Exterior derivative of η, Simon 1.11.) Since a is C^∞ it is differentiable (Lean: `ha.differentiable (by simp)`), hence so is η, and Mathlib's formula `extDeriv_apply` (SimonGMT `exteriorDerivative_apply`) gives for every x ∈ ℝⁿ and v = (v_0,…,v_m) ∈ (ℝⁿ)ⁿ:
   dη(x)(v) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i · D[y ↦ η(y)(v̂_i)](x)(v_i),
   where v̂_i := (v_0,…,v_{i−1},v_{i+1},…,v_m) (Lean: Fin.removeNth i v). Since η(y)(v̂_i) = a(y)·ι_j(v̂_i) and ι_j(v̂_i) does not depend on y, D[y ↦ η(y)(v̂_i)](x)(v_i) = Da(x)(v_i)·ι_j(v̂_i) (`fderiv_mul_const`). Hence
   dη(x)(v) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i · Da(x)(v_i) · dx(e_j, v̂_i).

5. (Evaluation at v = e.) Take v = e.
   (a) If i ≠ j, then e_j occurs among the entries of ê_i (it sits at position j or j−1 of ê_i), so the tuple (e_j, ê_i) has two equal entries and dx(e_j, ê_i) = 0 because dx is alternating (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq`, with the two positions 0 and k+1 where ê_i(k) = e_j, k given by `Fin.exists_succAbove_eq`).
   (b) If i = j, then (e_j, ê_j) = e ∘ σ, where σ = (cycleRange j)⁻¹ is the cyclic permutation moving position 0 to position j (`Fin.cons_removeNth_eq_comp_cycleRange_symm`); its sign is (−1)^j (`Fin.sign_cycleRange`, sign σ⁻¹ = sign σ). Since dx is alternating, dx(e ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·dx(e) = (−1)^j.
   Therefore dη(x)(e) = (−1)^j · D_j a(x) · (−1)^j = D_j a(x) for every x. (This is the printed identity dω_j = (D_j a) dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ, in view of Fact A.)

6. (dη = ω.) For each x ∈ ℝⁿ, dη(x) and ω(x) are n-covectors with dη(x)(e) = D_j a(x) = ω(x)(e) (the latter by hypothesis). By Fact A, dη(x) = dη(x)(e)·dx = ω(x)(e)·dx = ω(x). Hence the exterior derivative of η, as an element of Dⁿ(U) (Lean: exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η), equals ω (equality of subtypes by function extensionality).

7. (Conclusion, printed display (2).) By the definition of the boundary, T(ω) = T(dη) = (∂T)(η) = 0, because ∂T = 0 (Lean: T ω = T (exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η) = T.boundary η = (0 : GeometricCurrentOn U m) η = 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: dx := v ↦ det[v₁ … vₙ] has dx(e) = 1, and every n-covector α on ℝⁿ equals α(e)·dx (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det).
η := a·ι_{e_j}dx, ι_{e_j}dx(w) = dx(e_j, w) = (−1)^{j−1} dx¹∧⋯∧dx̂ʲ∧⋯∧dxⁿ, is the printed form ω_j and lies in D^{n−1}(U).
extDeriv_apply: dη(x)(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i Da(x)(v_i)·dx(e_j, v̂_i).
At v = e: terms i ≠ j vanish (repeated e_j); the term i = j has the cyclic sign (−1)^j, so dη(x)(e) = D_j a(x).
By the top-degree fact, dη = ω as test forms, hence T(ω) = T(dη) = ∂T(η) = 0.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean proposition agree, including arbitrary U and global coefficient equality. The determinant reduction, interior-product construction and permutation-sign computation establish dη = ω; zero boundary then gives T(ω) = 0. Compact support is preserved, and openness is unnecessary. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Globalization: local constancy on a connected open set gives T = c[[U]] (Steps 6–7 of Simon 2.34)
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n = m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open and connected and T ∈ D_n(U), and assume every x₀ ∈ U has r > 0 with B_r(x₀) ⊆ U and c ∈ ℝ such that T(ω) = c ∫ ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x₀). Then there is c ∈ ℝ with T(ω) = c ∫_U ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl (m + 1))), IsOpen U → IsConnected U → ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1), (∀ x₀ ∈ U, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ball x₀ r ⊆ U ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball x₀ r → T ω = c * ∫ x, (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) ∂volume) → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T ω = c * ∫ x in U, (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34, printed proof (p. 143), final clause “... on each ball B_ρ(x₀) with B̄_ρ(x₀) ⊆ U, and the result follows”, expanded as Steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof (overlapping balls, connectedness of U, partition of unity).

Setting and notation. m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open and connected, T ∈ D_n(U) (Lean: GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)), e = (e_1,…,e_n) the standard basis (Lean: e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (Lean: volume), spt = topological support (Lean: tsupport). Hypothesis:
(L) for every x₀ ∈ U there are r > 0 with B_r(x₀) ⊆ U and c ∈ ℝ such that T(ω) = c ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x₀).
Claim: there is c ∈ ℝ with T(ω) = c ∫_U ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U).

Proof.

1. (Choices.) Using (L), choose for every x₀ ∈ U a radius r(x₀) > 0 and a constant c(x₀) such that B(x₀) := B_{r(x₀)}(x₀) ⊆ U and T(ω) = c(x₀) ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) whenever ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ B(x₀).

2. (The form b dx.) Let dx := dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ, the n-covector v ↦ det[v_1 … v_n] (Lean: continuous alternating map with underlying map (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det), so dx(e) = 1. For b ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with compact support and spt b ⊆ U, the form [b] := (x ↦ b(x)·dx) lies in Dⁿ(U), spt [b] ⊆ spt b, and [b](x)(e) = b(x).

3. (Overlapping balls have equal constants — parent Step 6.) Let x₀, x₁ ∈ U with W := B(x₀) ∩ B(x₁) ≠ ∅. W is open; pick z ∈ W and δ > 0 with B_δ(z) ⊆ W. Let b be a normalized smooth bump: b ∈ C^∞, b ≥ 0, spt b = B̄_{δ/2}(z) ⊆ W, ∫ b dLⁿ = 1 (Lean: (ContDiffBump with centre z, rIn = δ/4, rOut = δ/2).normed volume; `integral_normed`, `tsupport_normed_eq`). Then [b] ∈ Dⁿ(U) and spt [b] ⊆ W ⊆ B(x₀) ∩ B(x₁). Applying Step 1 at x₀ and at x₁:
 c(x₀) = c(x₀) ∫ b = T([b]) = c(x₁) ∫ b = c(x₁).

4. (c is locally constant.) Let x₀ ∈ U and y ∈ B(x₀). Then y ∈ U, y ∈ B(y) (the centre of a ball of positive radius) and y ∈ B(x₀), so B(y) ∩ B(x₀) ≠ ∅ and c(y) = c(x₀) by Step 3. Thus the function c : U → ℝ is constant on the neighbourhood B(x₀) of each point x₀ of U, i.e. it is locally constant on U (with the subspace topology).

5. (Connectedness.) U is connected, so U ≠ ∅ and every locally constant function on U is constant (Mathlib: `IsLocallyConstant` on the subtype U together with `PreconnectedSpace U`, which follows from `IsConnected U`, gives `IsLocallyConstant.exists_eq_const`). Let c* be its value: c(x) = c* for all x ∈ U.

6. (Partition of unity — parent Step 7.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and K := spt ω, a compact subset of U. The open balls B(x), x ∈ K, cover K, so K ⊆ B(x_1) ∪ ⋯ ∪ B(x_N) for finitely many x_1,…,x_N ∈ K (N may be 0 when K = ∅). Choose a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to this finite open cover: χ_1,…,χ_N ∈ C^∞(ℝⁿ) with spt χ_k ⊆ B(x_k) and Σ_k χ_k(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib: `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate` for the closed set K and the open cover (B(x_k))_k, with the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝⁿ); smoothness of each χ_k as an ordinary C^∞ function follows from `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`). Each spt χ_k is closed and bounded, hence compact.

7. (Summation.) For each k let χ_kω be the form x ↦ χ_k(x)·ω(x). It is C^∞, spt χ_kω ⊆ spt χ_k ∩ spt ω, which is compact and contained in B(x_k) ⊆ U; so χ_kω ∈ Dⁿ(U) and spt χ_kω ⊆ B(x_k). Moreover ω = Σ_k χ_kω: for x ∈ K, Σ_k χ_k(x)ω(x) = ω(x); for x ∉ K, ω(x) = 0 and both sides vanish. By linearity of T, Step 1 at x_k and c(x_k) = c* (Step 5):
 T(ω) = Σ_k T(χ_kω) = Σ_k c* ∫ χ_k(x) ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) = c* ∫ Σ_k χ_k(x) ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) = c* ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x),
 where the integrands are continuous with compact support (hence integrable), so the finite sum may be exchanged with the integral.

8. (Integral over U.) Since spt ω ⊆ U, ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ U, hence ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) = ∫_U ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) (Mathlib `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero`). Therefore T(ω) = c* ∫_U ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U); take c := c*. ∎

Overlapping balls: a normalized bump b in the intersection gives c(x₀) = T(b dx) = c(x₁).
Hence c is locally constant on U, and constant (= c*) because U is connected.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to finitely many balls covering spt ω gives T(ω) = Σ_k T(χ_kω) = c*∫ω(x)(e)dLⁿ.
ω vanishes off U, so the integral over ℝⁿ equals the integral over U.

subproblem.title: Derivatives of a mollification are bounded by the L¹ norm
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, and q ∈ ℕ. Then there is a constant C such that ‖D^q(φ ∗ g)(x)‖ ≤ C ∫ |g| dLⁿ for every Lebesgue-integrable g : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every x ∈ ℝⁿ, where (φ ∗ g)(x) = ∫ φ(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) and D^q is the q-th Fréchet derivative.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (φ : Eucl n → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∀ q : ℕ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ g : Eucl n → ℝ, Integrable g volume → ∀ x : Eucl n, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ q (convolution φ g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x‖ ≤ C * ∫ y, |g y| ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 2.34 (p. 142): “D^β a^{(σ)} = (D^β φ^{(σ)}) ∗ a for each multi-index β, so if a_j → a in L¹(B_ρ(x₀)) ... then a_j^{(σ)} dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ → a^{(σ)} dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ in Dⁿ(U)”, together with the mollifier facts of Ch. 2, §2. This lemma is the quantitative form of that remark (all derivatives of a mollification are controlled by the L¹ norm of the mollified function), with the standard proof (differentiation under the integral sign) filled in.

Statement. Let n ∈ ℕ, φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, and q ∈ ℕ. Then there is C ∈ ℝ such that for every Lebesgue-integrable g : ℝⁿ → ℝ and every x ∈ ℝⁿ, ‖D^q(φ ∗ g)(x)‖ ≤ C ∫ |g| dLⁿ, where (φ ∗ g)(x) = ∫ φ(t) g(x − t) dLⁿ(t) (Lean: convolution φ g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, see `convolution_def`) and D^q is the q-th Fréchet derivative (Lean: iteratedFDeriv ℝ q; ‖·‖ is the norm of q-multilinear maps).

Proof. We prove a more general claim by induction on q, in which the kernel may be vector-valued; this is needed because the derivative of a real kernel is vector-valued.

1. (General convolutions.) For real normed spaces E, F (F complete), a continuous bilinear map L : E × ℝ → F (Lean: L : E →L[ℝ] ℝ →L[ℝ] F), a function f : ℝⁿ → E and g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ), put (f ∗_L g)(x) := ∫ L(f(t), g(x − t)) dt (Lean: convolution f g L volume). For E = F = ℝ and L = lsmul (L(s, t) = s t) this is φ ∗ g.

2. (Claim P(q).) For all E, F, L as in 1 and every B ≥ 0 with ‖L(u, t)‖ ≤ B ‖u‖ |t| for all u ∈ E, t ∈ ℝ; every C^∞ f : ℝⁿ → E with compact support; every S ∈ ℝ with ‖D^q f(t)‖ ≤ S for all t; every g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) and every x ∈ ℝⁿ:
 ‖D^q(f ∗_L g)(x)‖ ≤ B · S · ∫ |g| dLⁿ.
(The bound is phrased with an explicit constant B rather than the operator norm ‖L‖; this avoids norm-instance issues for the iterated bilinear maps of Step 4 and is mathematically equivalent.)

3. (P(0).) D^0 h(x) is h(x) (up to the isometry identifying E with 0-multilinear maps; `norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero`). By `convolution_def` and the norm bound for integrals (`norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`): ‖(f ∗_L g)(x)‖ ≤ ∫ ‖L(f(t), g(x − t))‖ dt ≤ ∫ B S |g(x − t)| dt = B S ∫ |g(x − t)| dt = B S ∫ |g| dLⁿ, since ‖f(t)‖ ≤ S and Lebesgue measure is invariant under t ↦ x − t (`integral_sub_left_eq_self`; t ↦ |g(x − t)| is integrable by `Integrable.comp_sub_left`).

4. (Derivative of a convolution.) If f is C^∞ with compact support and g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (in particular locally integrable), then f ∗_L g is differentiable at every point with D(f ∗_L g)(y) = ((Df) ∗_{L'} g)(y) (differentiation under the integral sign; Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left`), where Df : ℝⁿ → (ℝⁿ →L E) is again C^∞ with compact support (`ContDiff.fderiv_right`, `HasCompactSupport.fderiv`) and L' := L.precompL : (ℝⁿ →L E) × ℝ → (ℝⁿ →L F), L'(u, t)(v) = L(u v, t). L' satisfies the same bound: ‖L'(u, t)(v)‖ = ‖L(u v, t)‖ ≤ B ‖u v‖ |t| ≤ B ‖u‖ ‖v‖ |t| for all v, hence ‖L'(u, t)‖ ≤ B ‖u‖ |t| (`ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound`, `ContinuousLinearMap.precompL_apply`). Hence, as functions, D(f ∗_L g) = (Df) ∗_{L'} g.

5. (P(q) ⇒ P(q + 1).) Let f, S be as in P(q+1), i.e. ‖D^{q+1} f(t)‖ ≤ S for all t. subproblem.title: Mollifications of a test function converge with all derivatives uniformly
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, b : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, and let ψ_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) be continuous with ψ_k ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_k dLⁿ = 1 and spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0), where r_k → 0. Then for every q ∈ ℕ, D^q(ψ_k ∗ b) → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ as k → ∞, where (ψ ∗ b)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) b(x − t) dLⁿ(t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : Eucl n → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) b → HasCompactSupport b → ∀ (ψ : ℕ → Eucl n → ℝ) (r : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ k, Continuous (ψ k)) → (∀ k x, 0 ≤ ψ k x) → (∀ k, ∫ x, ψ k x ∂volume = 1) → (∀ k, tsupport (ψ k) ⊆ closedBall 0 (r k)) → Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ q : ℕ, TendstoUniformly (fun k x => iteratedFDeriv ℝ q (convolution (ψ k) b (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x) (fun x => iteratedFDeriv ℝ q b x) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 2.34 (p. 143), “Letting σ ↓ 0 we deduce that T = c_{ρ,x₀}[[B_ρ(x₀)]]”: the mollifications b^{(σ)} = φ^{(σ)} ∗ b of a test function b converge to b in the test-function topology (all derivatives uniformly); together with the mollifier facts of Ch. 2, §2. The standard proof is filled in, for an arbitrary nonnegative approximate identity (the mollifiers φ^{(σ)} are a special case).

Statement. Let n ∈ ℕ, b : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support, ψ_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) continuous with ψ_k ≥ 0, ∫ ψ_k dLⁿ = 1 and spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0), where r_k → 0. Then for every q ∈ ℕ, D^q(ψ_k ∗ b) → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ as k → ∞, where (ψ ∗ b)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) b(x − t) dLⁿ(t) (Lean: convolution (ψ k) b (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) and D^q = iteratedFDeriv ℝ q.

Proof.

1. (Preliminaries.) Each ψ_k is continuous, hence locally integrable. For each q, Ψ_q := D^q b : ℝⁿ → M_q (M_q the complete normed space of continuous q-multilinear maps (ℝⁿ)^q → ℝ) is C^∞ (`ContDiff.iteratedFDeriv_right`) with compact support (`HasCompactSupport.iteratedFDeriv`), hence uniformly continuous (`HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous`).

2. (Derivatives fall on b.) Claim: for every q and every locally integrable ψ, D^q(ψ ∗ b) = ψ ∗ Ψ_q as functions, i.e. D^q(ψ ∗ b)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) Ψ_q(x − t) dt (an M_q-valued integral; Lean: convolution ψ (iteratedFDeriv ℝ q b) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume). We use that a linear isometry e between complete normed spaces commutes with the Bochner integral, e(∫ φ) = ∫ e∘φ, with no integrability hypothesis (Mathlib `LinearIsometry.integral_comp_comm`, applied to e.toLinearIsometry).
 (q = 0) D^0 h(x) is the image of h(x) under the fixed linear isometry ℝ ≅ M_0 (`iteratedFDeriv_zero_eq_comp`, the inverse of `continuousMultilinearCurryFin0`), applied to h = ψ ∗ b and to b; pulling this isometry through the integral gives D^0(ψ ∗ b)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) Ψ_0(x − t) dt.
 (q → q + 1) Assume D^q(ψ ∗ b) = ψ ∗ Ψ_q. Since Ψ_q is C^∞ (in particular C¹) with compact support and ψ is locally integrable, ψ ∗ Ψ_q is differentiable with D(ψ ∗ Ψ_q)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) DΨ_q(x − t) dt (differentiation under the integral sign on the Ψ_q-side; Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right`, with the bilinear map (lsmul).precompR). Now D^{q+1}h(x) is the image of D(D^q h)(x) under the fixed linear isometry “uncurry” (the inverse of `continuousMultilinearCurryLeftEquiv`; Mathlib `iteratedFDeriv_succ_eq_comp_left`), for h = ψ ∗ b as well as for h = b (where it turns DΨ_q(y) into Ψ_{q+1}(y)). Pulling this isometry through the integral gives D^{q+1}(ψ ∗ b)(x) = ∫ ψ(t) Ψ_{q+1}(x − t) dt. This proves the claim for all q.

3. (Uniform estimate.) Fix q, write Ψ := Ψ_q and let δ > 0. By uniform continuity of Ψ (Step 1) there is s > 0 with ‖Ψ(y) − Ψ(z)‖ < δ/2 whenever |y − z| < s. Since r_k → 0, there is k₀ with r_k < s for all k ≥ k₀; then spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0) ⊆ B_s(0) (the open ball). Let k ≥ k₀ and x ∈ ℝⁿ. By Step 2 and ∫ψ_k = 1,
 D^q(ψ_k ∗ b)(x) − Ψ(x) = ∫ ψ_k(t) (Ψ(x − t) − Ψ(x)) dt,
 and since ψ_k ≥ 0 vanishes outside B_s(0) while ‖Ψ(x − t) − Ψ(x)‖ ≤ δ/2 for |t| < s,
 ‖D^q(ψ_k ∗ b)(x) − Ψ(x)‖ ≤ ∫ ψ_k(t) ‖Ψ(x − t) − Ψ(x)‖ dt ≤ δ/2 < δ.
 (Mathlib packages this estimate as `dist_convolution_le`: for f ≥ 0 with ∫ f = 1 and support f ⊆ ball 0 R (an open ball, here R := s), and g with ‖g(y) − z₀‖ ≤ ε on ball x₀ R, one has dist((f ∗ g)(x₀), z₀) ≤ ε; apply it with f = ψ_k, g = Ψ, x₀ = x, z₀ = Ψ(x), ε = δ/2.)

4. (Conclusion.) For every δ > 0 there is k₀ such that ‖D^q(ψ_k ∗ b)(x) − D^q b(x)‖ < δ for all k ≥ k₀ and all x ∈ ℝⁿ. Hence D^q(ψ_k ∗ b) → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ, for every q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ψ_q := D^q b is C^∞ with compact support, hence uniformly continuous.
Derivatives fall on b: D^q(ψ ∗ b) = ψ ∗ D^q b (hasFDerivAt_convolution_right; the curry isometries commute with the integral).
With ψ_k ≥ 0, ∫ψ_k = 1 and spt ψ_k inside B_s(0): ‖ψ_k ∗ Ψ − Ψ‖ ≤ sup_{|t|<s}‖Ψ(· − t) − Ψ‖ (dist_convolution_le).
r_k → 0 and uniform continuity give uniform convergence on ℝⁿ for each q.

subproblem.statement: Let μ be a finite measure on a measurable space α, F : (α → ℝ) → ℝ and C ∈ ℝ such that F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g), F(c f) = c F(f) and |F(f)| ≤ C ∫|f| dμ for all μ-integrable f, g and all c ∈ ℝ. Then there is a measurable θ : α → ℝ, bounded on all of α, with F(f) = ∫ f θ dμ for every μ-integrable f.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α), IsFiniteMeasure μ → ∀ (F : (α → ℝ) → ℝ) (C : ℝ), (∀ f g : α → ℝ, Integrable f μ → Integrable g μ → F (f + g) = F f + F g) → (∀ (c : ℝ) (f : α → ℝ), Integrable f μ → F (c • f) = c * F f) → (∀ f : α → ℝ, Integrable f μ → |F f| ≤ C * ∫ x, |f x| ∂μ) → ∃ θ : α → ℝ, Measurable θ ∧ (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x, |θ x| ≤ M) ∧ ∀ f : α → ℝ, Integrable f μ → F f = ∫ x, f x * θ x ∂μ

Source: Simon, Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 2.34 (p. 142), which invokes “the Riesz representation theorem for L¹(B_ρ(x₀))”: every bounded linear functional on L¹ of a finite measure is integration against a bounded measurable function ((L¹)* = L^∞). Simon cites this standard theorem without proof; the standard Radon–Nikodym proof is supplied below in the generality of an arbitrary finite measure (it is applied with μ = Lⁿ restricted to a ball).

Statement. Let (α, 𝔐) be a measurable space, μ a finite measure on α, F : (α → ℝ) → ℝ and C ∈ ℝ such that for all μ-integrable f, g and all c ∈ ℝ: (i) F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g); (ii) F(c f) = c F(f); (iii) |F(f)| ≤ C ∫|f| dμ. Then there is a measurable θ : α → ℝ with |θ(x)| ≤ M for all x (some M ∈ ℝ) such that F(f) = ∫ f θ dμ for every μ-integrable f.

Proof.

1. (Normalization.) Put C' := max(C, 0) ≥ 0; then |F(f)| ≤ C ∫|f| ≤ C' ∫|f| for integrable f, so (iii) holds with C' and we may assume C ≥ 0. By (ii) with c = 0, F(0) = 0. For integrable f, g we have f − g = f + (−1)·g, so F(f − g) = F(f) − F(g) by (i), (ii). Consequently, if f = g μ-a.e. (both integrable) then |F(f) − F(g)| = |F(f − g)| ≤ C ∫|f − g| dμ = 0, i.e. F(f) = F(g).

2. (The set function.) For measurable A ⊆ α the indicator 1_A is μ-integrable (μ(α) < ∞); put ν(A) := F(1_A). If A, B are disjoint measurable sets then 1_{A∪B} = 1_A + 1_B, so ν(A ∪ B) = ν(A) + ν(B) by (i); ν(∅) = F(0) = 0; and |ν(A)| ≤ C ∫ 1_A dμ = C μ(A) by (iii).

3. (Countable additivity.) Let (A_i)_{i∈ℕ} be pairwise disjoint measurable sets, A := ⋃_i A_i, S_N := ⋃_{i<N} A_i. By finite additivity, ν(A) − Σ_{i<N} ν(A_i) = ν(A \ S_N), and |ν(A \ S_N)| ≤ C μ(A \ S_N) → 0 as N → ∞, because A \ S_N decreases to ∅ and μ is finite (continuity from above). Moreover Σ_i |ν(A_i)| ≤ C Σ_i μ(A_i) = C μ(A) < ∞. Hence the series Σ_i ν(A_i) is absolutely, hence unconditionally, convergent with sum ν(A) (in Lean: HasSum, e.g. from summability of the norms and convergence of the partial sums). Setting ν(A) := 0 for non-measurable A, ν is a finite signed measure on (α, 𝔐) (Mathlib: `MeasureTheory.SignedMeasure`, i.e. `VectorMeasure α ℝ`). It is absolutely continuous with respect to μ: μ(A) = 0 implies |ν(A)| ≤ C μ(A) = 0.

4. (Radon–Nikodym.) μ is finite, hence σ-finite, and ν ≪ μ. By the Radon–Nikodym theorem for signed measures (Mathlib: `SignedMeasure.rnDeriv`, `SignedMeasure.integrable_rnDeriv`, `SignedMeasure.withDensityᵥ_rnDeriv_eq`) there is a measurable μ-integrable θ₀ : α → ℝ with ν(A) = ∫_A θ₀ dμ for every measurable A.

5. (Boundedness of the density.) Let A₊ := {x : θ₀(x) > C} (measurable). If μ(A₊) > 0, then ∫_{A₊} (θ₀ − C) dμ > 0, since the integrand is strictly positive on A₊ and A₊ has positive measure; that is, ν(A₊) = ∫_{A₊} θ₀ dμ > C μ(A₊), contradicting |ν(A₊)| ≤ C μ(A₊) from Step 2. So μ(A₊) = 0. Likewise A₋ := {θ₀ < −C} satisfies μ(A₋) = 0 (otherwise ν(A₋) < −C μ(A₋)). Define θ(x) := θ₀(x) if |θ₀(x)| ≤ C and θ(x) := 0 otherwise. Then θ is measurable, |θ(x)| ≤ C for every x (so M := C), θ = θ₀ μ-a.e., and therefore ν(A) = ∫_A θ dμ = ∫ 1_A θ dμ for every measurable A.

6. (Simple functions.) If s = Σ_{k=1}^{K} c_k 1_{A_k} with A_k measurable, then s is integrable and, by (i), (ii) and Step 5, F(s) = Σ_k c_k ν(A_k) = Σ_k c_k ∫ 1_{A_k} θ dμ = ∫ s θ dμ.

7. (All integrable functions.) For integrable f the product f θ is integrable (|f θ| ≤ C|f|, θ measurable). The property P(f): “F(f) = ∫ f θ dμ” holds for indicator functions c·1_A of measurable sets (Step 6), is preserved under sums of integrable functions (by (i) and linearity of the integral), is preserved under μ-a.e. equality (Step 1, and the integral only sees the a.e. class), and is closed in L¹: if ∫|f_k − f| dμ → 0 and P(f_k) for all k, then |F(f) − F(f_k)| = |F(f − f_k)| ≤ C ∫|f − f_k| → 0 and |∫ f θ − ∫ f_k θ| ≤ C ∫|f − f_k| → 0, so P(f). Since simple functions are dense in L¹(μ), P holds for every integrable f (in Mathlib this is exactly the induction principle `MeasureTheory.Integrable.induction`). Hence F(f) = ∫ f θ dμ for every μ-integrable f, with θ measurable and bounded. ∎

Remark (alternative route available in the pinned library). Steps 2–4 and the a.e. bound of Step 5 can be replaced by the Hilbert-space argument formalized in SimonGMT, module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.FiniteL1Dual (standard axioms only). By Step 1, F induces a bounded linear functional F̂ on the space Lp ℝ 1 μ of L¹ classes, F̂([f]) := F(f), with ‖F̂‖ ≤ C. If C = 0 then F = 0 on integrable functions and θ := 0 works. If C > 0, let ϑ := C·`finiteL1DualField μ (C⁻¹F̂)` (finiteL1DualField is ℝ-linear in its argument, being built from the linear map `InnerProductSpace.toDual.symm`); then F(f) = ∫ f ϑ dμ for every f ∈ L²(μ) (`finiteL1DualField_represents`, via the continuous inclusion L² ⊆ L¹ for finite μ), and |ϑ| ≤ C μ-a.e. (`finiteL1DualField_norm_le_one` applied to C⁻¹F̂, whose norm is ≤ 1). Indicators of measurable sets lie in L², so F(1_A) = ∫_A ϑ dμ for every measurable A. Truncating ϑ to an everywhere-bounded measurable representative θ as in Step 5 and concluding with Steps 6 and 7 gives the statement.

Radon–Nikodym gives θ₀ with ν(A) = ∫_A θ₀ dμ; |θ₀| ≤ C μ-a.e.; truncate to an everywhere-bounded measurable θ.
F(s) = ∫ sθ dμ for simple s; extend to all integrable f by L¹-density/closedness (Integrable.induction).

Source: Simon, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 and its printed proof (p. 142–143), the part ending with “T = c_{ρ,x₀}[[B_ρ(x₀)]] (c_{ρ,x₀} constant) on each ball B_ρ(x₀) with B̄_ρ(x₀) ⊂ U”; this is Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the parent proof, with the conclusion of its Step 2 (u(D_j a) = 0, i.e. T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0) taken as the hypothesis (H). As in the printed proof, the ball B_ρ(x₀) is fixed, R > ρ with B_R(x₀) ⊂ U, and the mollification parameter satisfies ε < R − ρ. Book n = m + 1. Erratum applied: the printed display (1) is garbled; it must read T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ) = ∫ a θ_ε dLⁿ for a ∈ L¹(B_ρ(x₀)) (the left side involves the mollified function a_ε = ϕ_ε ∗ a, as the preceding sentence of the printed proof defines F(a) = T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ)).

Setting and notation. m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open, T ∈ D_n(U) (Lean: GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)). e = (e_1,…,e_n) is the standard basis (Lean: e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), Lⁿ = Lebesgue measure (Lean: volume), D_j a(x) := Da(x)(e_j) (Lean: fderiv ℝ a x (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)), D^q the q-th derivative (Lean: iteratedFDeriv ℝ q), B_s(x) the open ball, B̄_s(x) the closed ball, “spt” the topological support (closure of {≠ 0}; Lean: tsupport). C_c^∞ denotes C^∞ functions ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support, C¹_c the C¹ functions with compact support. f ∗ g denotes the convolution (f ∗ g)(x) = ∫ f(t) g(x − t) dt (Lean: convolution f g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume). Hypothesis:
(H) T(ω) = 0 whenever ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), a ∈ C_c^∞ with spt a ⊆ U, j ∈ {1,…,n}, and ω(x)(e) = D_j a(x) for all x ∈ ℝⁿ.
Claim: for every x₀ ∈ U there are r > 0 with B_r(x₀) ⊆ U and c ∈ ℝ such that T(ω) = c ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x₀).
Sibling lemmas used: constancy_riesz_l1_dual_bounded_density (Riesz representation (L¹)* = L^∞ for a finite measure), constancy_mollifier_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le_integral (for φ ∈ C_c^∞ and each q there is C_q with |D^q(φ ∗ g)(x)| ≤ C_q ∫|g| for all integrable g and all x), constancy_approx_identity_iteratedFDeriv_tendstoUniformly (for b ∈ C_c^∞ and continuous ψ_k ≥ 0 with ∫ψ_k = 1, spt ψ_k ⊆ B̄_{r_k}(0), r_k → 0: D^q(ψ_k ∗ b) → D^q b uniformly on ℝⁿ for each q).

Proof.

0. (Radii.) Fix x₀ ∈ U. U is open, so B_{R₀}(x₀) ⊆ U for some R₀ > 0. Put R := R₀/2 and ρ := r := R/2. Then K := B̄_R(x₀) ⊆ B_{R₀}(x₀) ⊆ U is compact, r > 0, and B := B_ρ(x₀) = B_r(x₀) ⊆ U. For 0 < ε < R − ρ = R/2 we have ρ + ε < R.

1. (Reduction to a distribution — parent Step 1.)
 (1a) Let dx := dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ be the n-covector v ↦ det[v_1 … v_n] (Lean: the continuous alternating map whose underlying alternating map is (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det; continuity: the determinant of the coordinate matrix depends continuously on v, `Continuous.matrix_det`). dx(e) = 1 (`Module.Basis.det_self`), and every α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝⁿ) equals α(e)·dx, because the alternating n-linear forms on an n-dimensional space are the multiples of the determinant (`AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det`).
 (1b) For a ∈ C_c^∞ with spt a ⊆ U let [a] := a·dx, the form x ↦ a(x)·dx; it is C^∞, spt [a] ⊆ spt a, so [a] ∈ Dⁿ(U), and [a](x)(e) = a(x). Put u(a) := T([a]). Since [a + b] = [a] + [b] and [ca] = c[a], u is linear.
 (1c) For ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) put a_ω(x) := ω(x)(e). Then a_ω is C^∞ (ω composed with the continuous linear evaluation at e), spt a_ω ⊆ spt ω (compact, ⊆ U), and ω = [a_ω] by (1a). Hence T(ω) = u(a_ω).
 (1d) (Derivatives of [a].) D^q[a](x) is the image of D^q a(x) under the fixed continuous linear map t ↦ t·dx (`ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_comp_left`), so ‖D^q[a](x)‖ ≤ ‖dx‖·‖D^q a(x)‖ and D^q[a_k] → D^q[a] uniformly whenever D^q a_k → D^q a uniformly.
 (1e) (Continuity of u.) If a_k, a ∈ C_c^∞ have spt ⊆ K' for one compact K' ⊆ U and D^q a_k → D^q a uniformly on ℝⁿ for every q ∈ ℕ, then u(a_k) → u(a): by (1d), [a_k − a] → 0 in the sense of `TestFormOnConverges` (all supports in K', every derivative uniformly), and the continuity axiom of T (`GeometricCurrentOn.continuous'`) gives u(a_k) − u(a) = T([a_k − a]) → 0.
 (1f) (Hypothesis (H) in terms of u.) If a ∈ C_c^∞ with spt a ⊆ U and j ∈ {1,…,n}, then D_j a ∈ C_c^∞, spt D_j a ⊆ spt a ⊆ U, and [D_j a](x)(e) = D_j a(x); so (H) gives u(D_j a) = T([D_j a]) = 0. [This is the printed identity T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0, encoded in (H).]
 (1g) It therefore suffices to find c with u(b) = c ∫ b dLⁿ for every b ∈ C_c^∞ with spt b ⊆ B: then for ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B = B_r(x₀), a_ω ∈ C_c^∞ with spt a_ω ⊆ B, and T(ω) = u(a_ω) = c ∫ a_ω dLⁿ = c ∫ ω(x)(e) dLⁿ(x).

2. (Mollifiers, as in §2 of Ch. 2.) For ε > 0 let ϕ_ε ∈ C_c^∞ with ϕ_ε ≥ 0, ϕ_ε(−x) = ϕ_ε(x), ∫ ϕ_ε dLⁿ = 1 and spt ϕ_ε = B̄_ε(0) (e.g. ϕ_ε(x) = ε^{−n}ϕ(x/ε) for a fixed mollifier ϕ; Lean: the normalized `ContDiffBump` centred at 0 with rIn = ε/2, rOut = ε, from Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed: `contDiff_normed`, `continuous_normed`, `nonneg_normed`, `normed_neg`, `integral_normed`, `tsupport_normed_eq`). For g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) let g_ε := ϕ_ε ∗ g. Facts:
 (M1) g_ε ∈ C^∞ (`HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left`, differentiation under the integral sign).
 (M2) If g = 0 outside a set S, then g_ε = 0 outside S + B̄_ε(0) (`MeasureTheory.support_convolution_subset`).
 (M3) For each q there is C_q(ε) ≥ 0 with |D^q g_ε(x)| ≤ C_q(ε) ∫|g| dLⁿ for all x and all g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) — sibling lemma constancy_mollifier_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le_integral with φ = ϕ_ε (replace C_q by max(C_q, 0)).
 (M4) If g ∈ C¹_c then D_j(g_ε) = (D_j g)_ε (the derivative falls on g: `HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right`, evaluated at e_j).
 (M5) If g ∈ C_c^∞ and ε_k ↓ 0 then D^q(g_{ε_k}) → D^q g uniformly on ℝⁿ for every q — sibling lemma constancy_approx_identity_iteratedFDeriv_tendstoUniformly with ψ_k = ϕ_{ε_k}, r_k = ε_k.

3. (Printed display (1), corrected.) Fix ε with 0 < ε < R/2. For a function a integrable on B put ã := 1_B·a ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (a extended by zero). By (M1), (M2), ã_ε ∈ C^∞ and ã_ε = 0 outside B + B̄_ε(0) ⊆ B_{ρ+ε}(x₀), so spt ã_ε ⊆ B̄_{ρ+ε}(x₀) ⊆ K ⊆ U and ã_ε ∈ C_c^∞. Define F(a) := u(ã_ε) for a integrable on B (and F(a) := 0 otherwise; these values play no role). Since a ↦ ã ↦ ã_ε and u are linear, F(a + b) = F(a) + F(b) and F(c a) = c F(a) for a, b integrable on B and c ∈ ℝ.
 F is bounded on L¹(B). The printed proof argues: if a_j → a in L¹(B) then, by (M3), every derivative of (ã_j)_ε converges uniformly to that of ã_ε with all supports in K, so T((ã_j)_ε dx) → T(ã_ε dx) by (1e); “thus the functional F is a bounded linear functional on L¹(B_ρ(x₀))”. Explicitly: by the finite-order estimate for currents (SimonGMT `GeometricCurrentOn.exists_compact_derivative_bound`, module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FixedSupportCurrentTopology, applied to T and the compact K ⊆ U) there are N ∈ ℕ and C₀ > 0 with |T(ω)| ≤ C₀·D whenever ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ K, D ≥ 0 and ‖D^q ω(x)‖ ≤ D for all q ≤ N and x ∈ K. For ω = [ã_ε], (1d) and (M3) give ‖D^q[ã_ε](x)‖ ≤ ‖dx‖·C_q(ε)·∫|ã| = ‖dx‖·C_q(ε)·∫_B|a|, so with C := C₀‖dx‖·max_{q≤N} C_q(ε):
 |F(a)| ≤ C ∫_B |a| dLⁿ for every a integrable on B.
 [Equivalently, without the finite-order estimate: if no such C existed, choose a_k with |F(a_k)| > k²∫_B|a_k|; then ∫_B|a_k| > 0 (otherwise ã_k = 0 a.e., (ã_k)_ε ≡ 0 and F(a_k) = 0) and b_k := a_k/(k∫_B|a_k|) has ∫_B|b_k| = 1/k → 0 but |F(b_k)| > k, contradicting the sequential continuity just shown.]

It yields a measurable θ_ε : ℝⁿ → ℝ, bounded by some M everywhere, with
 (1) u(ã_ε) = F(a) = ∫_B a θ_ε dLⁿ for every a integrable on B.
 This is the corrected printed display (1).

4. (Printed display (2); θ_ε is constant.) Let a ∈ C¹_c with spt a ⊆ B and j ∈ {1,…,n}. Then ã = a; D_j a is continuous with spt D_j a ⊆ spt a ⊆ B, hence integrable on B with (D_j a)~ = D_j a; a_ε ∈ C_c^∞ with spt a_ε ⊆ K ⊆ U (Step 3); and (D_j a)_ε = D_j(a_ε) by (M4). Using (1) for D_j a and (1f) for the C_c^∞ function a_ε:
 (2) ∫_B (D_j a) θ_ε dLⁿ = u((D_j a)_ε) = u(D_j(a_ε)) = 0, j = 1,…,n.
 [In the printed notation: with ω_j = (−1)^{j−1} a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{j−1}∧dx^{j+1}∧⋯∧dxⁿ one has dω_j = (D_j a)_ε dx, and (2) reads T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0.]
 Thus the bounded measurable (hence locally integrable on B) function θ_ε has vanishing weak partial derivatives in the ball B, tested against all C¹_c functions supported in B. As in the printed proof, θ_ε is Lⁿ-a.e. constant on B: for 0 < σ < ρ and x ∈ B_{ρ−σ}(x₀), the function y ↦ ϕ_σ(x − y) is C_c^∞ with spt ⊆ B̄_σ(x) ⊆ B and D_{y_j}[ϕ_σ(x − y)] = −(D_jϕ_σ)(x − y); so with θ̃_ε := 1_B θ_ε, differentiation under the integral sign and (2) give D_j(ϕ_σ ∗ θ̃_ε)(x) = ∫ (D_jϕ_σ)(x − y) θ_ε(y) dy = −∫_B D_j[ϕ_σ(x − ·)] θ_ε dLⁿ = 0.
